text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
CORN SALE - Exporters reported the sale of 120,000 tonnes of U.S. corn to unknown destinations for delivery during this marketing year, U.S. Agriculture Department said Friday.
- Taiwan's FGEP corn-buying group bought one 54,000-tonne shipment of U.S. No.2 corn from Marubeni at a tender for March delivery on Friday, local traders said.
- South Korea's National Livestock Cooperatives Federation bought 105,000 tonnes of corn. It bought 52,500 tonnes each from Mitsui and South Korea's Taihan Sugar Corp.

WHEAT SALE - The Taiwan Flour Mills Association bought three shipments of U.S. wheat totalling 86,000 tonnes at a tender on Friday, traders said. Each shipment contains Dark Northern Spring, Hard Red Winter and White Wheat and all are slated for delivery from the Pacific Northwest for January and February shipment, traders said.
BARLEY SALE - Cyprus's Grain Commission on Friday accepted Soufflet Paris's tender for 25,000 tonnes of barley at $146.89 per tonne. Prices include C and F and shipment is scheduled for January.
SOYOIL SALE - Tunisia bought 18,000 tonnes optional origin soyoil for February shipment, several U.S. exporters said.

WHEAT TENDER - Philippine firms on Friday rejected tenders for the supply of 35,000 tonnes U.S. wheat for February shipment, traders involved in the deal said. "We rejected all offers because the average offer of $187 per tonne FOB was too high," an official of one of the buying firms said.

- Armenia is seeking about 65,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat under the PL 480 program for January 23-February 6 delivery, its U.S. export agent said. Offers are to be submitted on January 15 and will be valid until January 16.

WHEAT TENDERS - Yemen has postponed a tender for soft wheat grain and soft wheat flour initially scheduled for January 7 until January 14, grain traders said. Yemen is seeking 200,000 tonnes of European or U.S soft wheat flour for shipment by June. Within the EU Yemen is seeking French, Dutch, German or Belgian flour. It also seeks 200,000 tonnes of optional soft wheat for shipment between June and August.
- Lebanon's economy ministry plans to buy 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat later this month, the Cereals and Sugar Beet Office said. "It will be Hard Red Winter No.2," the official said.
WHEAT TENDERS - Pakistan will tender Jan 12 for 315,000 tonnes of Australian white milling wheat and U.S. soft white wheat. Shipment was slated for February 1-28.

- Bangladesh seeks 100,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 wheat or Australian standard or better Canadian winter red/spring wheat for shipment by February 21. Offers are to be opened January 18 and the results announced two to three days later.
SOYMEAL TENDER - South Korea's Korea Feed Association will invite tenders for 125,000 tonnes of soymeal on Monday. The tenders were divided into four positions for March 20.

SOYBEAN MEAL TENDER - The Commodity Credit Corp said it seeks offers from exporters for 2,650 tonnes of 48 percent protein soybean meal for donation to Guatemala. Shipment is slated for between January 30 and February 25, 1997. Offers are due on January 14 at 1400 CST.
RICE TENDER - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foostuffs is seeking to buy 12,000 tonnes of white rice for March shipment. Results would be Feb 13.

MARKET TALK - Algeria is expected to tap world markets for soft wheat soon after failing to buy 100,000 tonnes of milling wheat last month, European grain traders said on Friday. There was, however, no official word that a tender was in the making. Exporters said Algeria may be in the market during the first days of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan that started on Friday to cover import requirements for February and March.
